subject: B09DF372555FE0EF51DAE5C0119AD51E
introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá was born in Tehran in 1844, saw his father taken to the Síyáh-Chál when he was eight, and grew up in exile in Baghdad. This small guide gathers what he said about those years, mostly at table to pilgrims: a neighbour’s birds, an illness that should have killed him, an errand through hostile streets, his visit to the prison, a hunt he gave up. They are told lightly. The Gospels give one such glimpse of Jesus, a boy among the doctors in the temple; Samuel’s childhood and Timothy’s “from a child” are the other scriptural childhoods; Wordsworth’s line is the modern conviction that such memories matter.
questions: Which of these memories seems to you to have shaped the man?
Why do religious traditions preserve so little about the childhood of their central figures, and what do the few stories do?
What did the child see at the prison, and what did he do with it afterwards?

outside.why: Particulars of earliest childhood stick in the memory. Wordsworth: the Child is father of the Man.
A neighbour who was a bird fancier. Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.
“While I nursed with my mother’s milk I received truth.” From a child thou hast known the holy scriptures.
And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom.
The days when I came to thee as a child with love. The child Samuel: speak; for thy servant heareth.
An elderly man who lived near our house. Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man.
At seven, consumption, and no hope of recovery; and then recovery. I have heard thy prayer, I have seen thy tears: behold, I will add unto thy days.
As a little child, sent to carry a message. Wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?
A small lad in Baghdad, active in the discussions. They found him sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
Taken as a child to the prison to see his father. Jacob mourned for his son many days, and refused to be comforted.
A youthful wish to hunt, given up. A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast.
When I was a child, I spake as a child; when I became a man, I put away childish things. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells these stories as an old man, with evident pleasure. What does he seem not to have put away?

shortfall: Readings 3, 5 and 11 are a greeting, a place of birth and a feat of marksmanship.
